# Project notes

{{RULE}}

## Project overview

This is a small utility library consumed by a handful of internal services.
It ships as CommonJS; there is no build step and no transpiler.
Keep the dependency count at zero — everything here is hand-rolled on purpose.
The public surface is deliberately tiny; most helpers stay private to their module.
Node 22 is the only supported runtime. No browser support is planned.

## Repository layout

- `src/` — library modules, one concern per file.
- `tests/` — `node:test` suites, one file per module.
- `scripts/` — maintenance scripts, run with plain `node`.
- `fixtures/` — sample data used by the test suites.
Files outside these directories are configuration and can be ignored day to day.

## Commands

- `node --test tests/` — run the full suite.
- `node --test --test-name-pattern <re>` — run a subset.
- `node scripts/bench.js` — micro-benchmarks for the hot paths.
- `node scripts/lint-imports.js` — check import ordering.
There is no watch mode; re-run the suite manually after edits.

## Code style

- Two-space indentation, double quotes, semicolons on.
- `const` by default; `let` only when reassignment is unavoidable.
- Modules start with `"use strict";` even though CommonJS implies it in Node.
- Keep functions under ~40 lines; extract a helper before nesting a third level.
- Prefer early returns over `else` chains.
- Destructure at the call boundary, not deep inside a function body.

## Naming

- Files are lower-kebab-case; exported symbols are lowerCamelCase.
- Boolean-returning helpers start with `is`, `has`, or `can`.
- Avoid abbreviations except `n` for counts in tight numeric helpers.
- Private module-level helpers get a leading underscore only when a public sibling shares the name.

## Testing conventions

- Every exported function gets at least one happy-path and one edge-case test.
- Use `assert.deepStrictEqual` over loose equality in all new tests.
- Test names read as sentences: `it rounds half away from zero`.
- Fixtures live in `fixtures/` and are loaded relative to the test file.
- Never let a test depend on wall-clock time; inject clocks where needed.

## Git conventions

- Branch names: `feat/<slug>`, `fix/<slug>`, or `chore/<slug>`.
- Commits are imperative mood, under 72 characters in the subject.
- Squash-merge feature branches; keep main linear.
- Rebase local work before opening a review; never force-push a shared branch.

## Performance notes

- The hot paths are the string helpers; avoid allocating in loops there.
- Regexes used in hot paths are hoisted to module scope and reused.
- Micro-optimizations need a benchmark diff from `scripts/bench.js` to land.
- Prefer a single pass over chained array methods when the input can be large.

## Dependency policy

- Runtime dependencies are not accepted; the library stays zero-dependency.
- Dev tooling beyond Node's built-ins needs a strong justification in review.
- Vendored snippets carry a comment with their origin and license.

## Review etiquette

- Reviews focus on behavior and API shape, not formatting nits.
- A single approving review is enough for helpers; API changes need two.
- Leave the branch in a merge-ready state: suite green, no stray debug files.
- Large mechanical renames go in their own commit so the interesting diff stays small.
